author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Pentagon is discussing a loan of about $5 billion to AI cloud startup Fluidstack, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday, as the United States looks to expand the domestic supply chain behind data centers.

Reuters said the potential financing would come from the Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital. The money would support manufacturing capacity for selected data-center components rather than directly fund construction of a new AI facility, according to the report.
Neither the Defense Department nor Fluidstack immediately commented to Reuters. The talks therefore do not represent a completed loan, and the final amount or terms could change.

The proposal follows a national-emergency order issued last month that restricted some foreign equipment used by the U.S. power grid. The Office of Strategic Capital has also backed companies in areas such as rare-earth materials and drones. A Fluidstack loan would extend that industrial-policy approach to the computing and electrical hardware needed for large AI systems, where shortages or foreign dependence could slow data-center deployment.
dek: The proposed financing would support domestic production of data-center components as Washington treats AI infrastructure as a strategic supply-chain priority.
headline: Pentagon discusses $5 billion Fluidstack loan, WSJ reports
